answer.rationale: The 18% spend mandate and 14-day contract expiry create a constrained decision window. Memory_c2 documents successful low-cost vendor switching with quick onboarding and accurate invoicing—directly relevant to validating the low-cost quote's credibility. Memory_c4 shows negotiation recovered margin, but the incumbent's silence on renewal suggests limited negotiating room here. The low-cost vendor quote meets the 18% mandate alone, eliminating budget pressure. However, the assembly line runs at 94% capacity with no buffer—this is a material delivery risk if the vendor experiences any onboarding friction or quality variance. Verifying c2 and c4 will confirm whether prior low-cost switches succeeded under similar constraints and whether negotiation leverage remains. Switching primary vendor is the only action that meets the financial mandate decisively within the timeline. The standard_experiment scale allows staged volume commitment to validate quality and delivery performance before full commitment, mitigating the thin operational buffer.
